2027-01-01.title: The Holy Name of Jesus (Circumcision of our Lord) · New Year's Day
2027-01-01.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: God changes Abram's name and gives the covenant of circumcision
I have called you by name, you are mine
The name that is above every name
2027-01-01.alt: Also the First Friday of Nativity, which in this calendar is the last Friday of Nativity: the Divine Motherhood of Mary (Exodus 15:11–21; Acts 1:12–14; Romans 16:17–20, 25–27; Luke 1:39–45). New Year readings: Exodus 23:14–17; Isaiah 52:7–12; Ephesians 4:17–24; Matthew 6:25–34. Weekday readings: Hebrews 1:1–4; John 1:14–18.
2027-01-01.verse: She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
theo: On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised and “he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.” The Syro-Malabar Church begins the civil year with this feast of the Holy Name. In the first reading God changes Abram's name to Abraham and gives him the covenant sign; a new name means a new mission. Through Isaiah God says to his people: “I have called you by name, you are mine.” Names in the Bible are not labels; they reveal who someone is before God.

The name Jesus, Yeshua, means “the LORD saves”. The angel explains it to Joseph: “he will save his people from their sins.” And St Paul sings the hymn of Philippians: the Son emptied himself, took the form of a slave, became obedient to death on a cross, “Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend.” The way to the exalted Name passed through humility and the Cross.

Today is also the last Friday of the Nativity season, kept as the Divine Motherhood of Mary. The woman who gave the Child his human flesh is the Mother of God; she stands with the Apostles in prayer at the beginning of the Church (Acts 1:14). As the new year opens, the Church places on our lips the Name in which there is salvation, and under our eyes the Mother who keeps us close to her Son.
conn: Circumcision on the eighth day.
Genesis 17:12 commands it as the sign of the covenant. By submitting to the Law, the Son of God enters fully into the history of his people (Galatians 4:4).
Naming.
In Israel the father named the child. Joseph obeys the angel and names him Jesus, thus legally adopting him into David's line (Matthew 1:25).
The Name in Syriac prayer.
The East Syriac liturgy is full of the name Isho Mshiha, Jesus the Messiah. The Malayalam ഈശോ comes from this Syriac form.
Prayer of the Name.
The Jesus Prayer, “Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner”, is loved in the Christian East as a way of praying without ceasing.
Divine Motherhood.
The Syro-Malabar calendar keeps the Divine Motherhood of Mary on the last Friday of the Nativity season. The Council of Ephesus (431) confessed Mary as Mother of God.
New Year.
The Church blesses time. Exodus 23:14–17 tells Israel to keep festivals for the Lord through the year: the calendar itself becomes worship.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana the Name of Jesus is invoked again and again. We receive the One whose Name means “the Lord saves”.
Begin the year by receiving Holy Communion with this prayer: Jesus, be my Saviour this year in every day.
outline: Ask: who gave you your name, and what does it mean?
God names Abraham and calls his people his own.
The meaning of the name Jesus.
Humility and the Cross lead to exaltation.
Joseph whispering the name Jesus over the Child.
live: Pray the Name
Pray the Jesus Prayer slowly ten times each morning this year.
Honour the Name (Philippians 2:10)
Bow your head at the name of Jesus, and never use it carelessly.
Bless the year
Gather your family tonight and consecrate the new year to Jesus under the protection of Mary.
Know your name
Find out the meaning of your baptismal name and the saint you are named after.
fathers: The name of Jesus is honey in the mouth, music in the ear, joy in the heart.
His name is a treasure: whoever calls on it is rich, and whoever holds it is not poor.
magis: Prayer to Jesus by name; the Jesus Prayer.
Mary, Mother of God and Mother of the Church.
Mary in the mystery of Christ and the Church.
saints: 2 Jan: First Saturday of Nativity. 3 Jan: Second Sunday of Nativity; St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. 6 Jan: Denha.
2027-01-01.prayer: Lord Jesus, your Name means “the Lord saves”. At the beginning of this new year we bow before your holy Name, which is above every name. Write your Name on our hearts, save us from our sins, and keep us all through this year under the mantle of your Mother, the Mother of God. To you be glory with the Father and the Holy Spirit, now and for ever. Amen.

2027-01-03.title: Second Sunday of Nativity
2027-01-03.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The skin of Moses' face shone
Speak, for your servant is listening
Present your bodies as a living sacrifice
I must be in my Father's house
2027-01-03.alt: 3 January is also the feast of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara (Genesis 12:1–4; Isaiah 44:1–4; 1 Peter 4:12–19; Matthew 5:1–12); where it is kept, follow the local direction. The feast of Denha is on Wednesday 6 January: remind the faithful.
2027-01-03.verse: And Jesus increased in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.
theo: The two Sundays of Nativity look at the Child growing up. Today's readings are all set in the presence of God. Moses comes down from forty days on Sinai and does not know “that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.” The boy Samuel, sleeping in the temple where the ark was, hears the Lord call him three times, until he learns to answer: “Speak, for your servant is listening.” Those who stay near God are changed by him and learn to listen.

In the Gospel Jesus, at twelve, goes up to Jerusalem for the Passover and stays behind. After three days of anxious searching, Mary and Joseph find him in the Temple, “sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.” His first recorded words are: “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” The Son knows who his Father is. Yet he goes down to Nazareth “and was obedient to them”, and grows “in wisdom and in years, and in divine and human favor.” Holiness and ordinary obedience belong together.

St Paul turns this into a programme for every Christian: “present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship. Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your minds.” The Temple is now our life offered to God. The feast of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara today shows a son of our Church who lived this: priest, founder, educator, a man of prayer whose face, like Moses', shone with God among his people.
conn: Moses' veil.
Exodus 34 says Moses veiled his face after speaking to the people. St Paul reads this in 2 Corinthians 3: in Christ the veil is removed and we are transformed from glory to glory.
Samuel in the temple.
Samuel was dedicated by his mother Hannah (1 Samuel 1). The lamp of God had not yet gone out: God speaks before the darkness falls.
Bar mitzvah?
The later Jewish rite of coming of age at thirteen is not described in Luke, but at twelve Jesus is close to the age of religious responsibility.
Three days.
Mary and Joseph search for three days before finding Jesus. The Fathers saw a hint of the three days of the Passion before the Resurrection.
First words.
Jesus' first words in Luke speak of his Father; his last words on the Cross also speak to the Father (Luke 23:46).
St Chavara.
St Kuriakose Elias Chavara (1805–1871), co-founder of the CMI and founder of the CMC congregations, pioneered schools beside churches and printed Malayalam books at Mannanam. Canonised in 2014.
altar: The Holy Qurbana is our presence in the Father's house. Like the boy Jesus, we are where we belong.
At the offertory we place ourselves on the altar as a living sacrifice (Romans 12:1). We return home transformed.
outline: Ask: have you ever lost a child in a crowd? What did you feel?
“I must be in my Father's house.”
live: Listen like Samuel (1 Samuel 3:10)
Begin your prayer this week with the words: Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.
Find Jesus in the Father's house
Make a short visit to the church on a weekday.
Obedience at home (Luke 2:51)
Children: obey your parents promptly this week. Parents: listen to your children's questions.
Imitate St Chavara
Support a poor child's education this year.
fathers: The Lord at twelve begins to show that he is the Son of God, and yet he is subject to his parents, so that we may learn obedience.
He who was greater than the Temple sat in the Temple, listening and asking, so that the teachers might learn who was teaching them.
magis: The hidden life at Nazareth; the finding in the Temple.
Listening to the Word, like Samuel.
saints: 3 Jan: St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. 6 Jan: Denha (Baptism of the Lord). 8 Jan: St John the Baptist (First Friday of Denha).
2027-01-03.prayer: Lord Jesus, at twelve you were found in your Father's house, listening and asking. Then you went down to Nazareth and were obedient. Teach us to listen like Samuel, to shine with God's presence like Moses, and to offer our lives as a living sacrifice. Through the prayers of St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, make our homes and our parish places where you grow in us. Glory to you with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

2027-01-06.title: Denha · The Epiphany and Baptism of our Lord
2027-01-06.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: The Lord descends upon Mount Sinai
I will pour out my spirit on all flesh
Grace revealed through the appearing of our Saviour
You are my Son, the Beloved
2027-01-06.alt: Important feast and day of obligation. The Third Qudasha (anaphora) is used in the Holy Qurbana. Beginning of the Season of Denha.
2027-01-06.verse: And a voice came from heaven, “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
theo: Denha is a Syriac word meaning dawn, rising, manifestation. The Eastern Churches celebrate on this day not first the Magi but the Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan, because there the whole mystery of God shone out: the Son in the water, the Spirit descending like a dove, the Father's voice from heaven. “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.” At the Jordan the Holy Trinity is revealed, and the public ministry of Jesus begins. The Sun of Justice rises over the world.

The readings show God coming down. At Sinai “the LORD had descended upon it in fire”, with thunder, smoke and trembling, and the people had to keep their distance. At the Jordan the heavens are “torn apart”, and God comes close in gentleness: the Spirit descends like a dove upon a man standing in the water among sinners. Joel's promise begins to be fulfilled: “I will pour out my spirit on all flesh.” What was terrifying at Sinai becomes intimate at the Jordan.

Jesus did not need baptism; he was without sin. He went down into the water to sanctify the waters for us and to stand with sinners. St Paul tells Timothy to “rekindle the gift of God that is within you”, for grace “has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light.” Our ancestors' customs, the lamps on plantain stems with the cry “El Paiya”, God is light, and the night bath recalling the Jordan, were ways of saying: our Baptism made us children of light. Denha calls each of us to remember our Baptism and to live as beloved sons and daughters.
conn: Denha.
Syriac for dawn or rising. The feast is called Denha (Epiphany) in the East Syriac tradition, and in Kerala popularly Pindikuthi in the north and Rakkuli in the south.
Pindikuthi.
Lamps were fixed on a plantain stem (pindi) and the family processed around it crying “El Paiya”, a Syriac-Malayalam cry meaning God is light. Christ is the light of the world.
Rakkuli.
On the eve, families bathed in rivers or ponds at night (rakkuli, “night bath”), recalling the Jordan. It was a religious act of remembering Baptism, not a magical rite.
Sinai and Jordan.

Both are theophanies. At Sinai God gives the Law in fire; at the Jordan he gives his Son and his Spirit. Mark says the heavens were “torn apart” (schizō), the same verb used for the Temple curtain at Jesus' death (Mark 15:38).
Blessing of water.
In many Eastern Churches water is solemnly blessed at Denha, because Christ sanctified the waters by his baptism (CCC 1224).
The Fridays of Denha.

On the Fridays of this season the Church remembers the great witnesses of Christ: John the Baptist, Peter and Paul, the Evangelists, Stephen, the Greek and Syrian Fathers, and finally all the faithful departed.
altar: The Third Qudasha is used today, with its rich prayers on the Holy Trinity. At the Jordan the Trinity was revealed; at the altar the Trinity gives us the Body and Blood of the Son by the Spirit.
In Baptism we went down into the water with Christ; in the Holy Qurbana we are fed as beloved children.
outline: Ask: do you know the date of your Baptism?
From Sinai's fire to the Jordan's dove.
Jesus sanctifies the waters for us.
Live as beloved children of light.
A plantain stem with small lamps, and a family crying “El Paiya”.
live: Remember your Baptism
Find out your baptismal date and keep it like a birthday.
Bless with holy water
Keep holy water at home and bless yourself and your children each night.
Rekindle the gift (2 Timothy 1:6)
Use one gift God gave you to serve the parish this month.
Keep the custom
Teach children the meaning of Pindikuthi and Rakkuli.
fathers: Fire and Spirit are in the river in which you were baptised: the Jordan received the One who is fire, and the waters were made holy.
Christ is baptised: let us go down with him, so that we may also rise with him.
magis: Baptism makes us children of God and members of the Church.
The Eastern liturgy as a feast of light and theophany.
saints: 8 Jan: First Friday of Denha, St John the Baptist. 10 Jan: Second Sunday of Denha.
2027-01-06.prayer: O Christ, Sun of Justice, today you rose upon the world at the Jordan. The Father bore witness to you and the Spirit descended upon you. Sanctify us who were baptised into you; rekindle in us the gift of God; and let us live as beloved children of light. To you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be praise and glory, now and always and for ever. Amen.

2027-01-02.title: First Saturday of Nativity
2027-01-02.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: You have been enriched in him in speech and knowledge
Anna speaks of the child; Jesus grows in wisdom
2027-01-02.verse: The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom; and the favor of God was upon him.
theo: Luke ends the story of the Presentation with an old woman: Anna, a prophet, widowed after seven years of marriage and now eighty-four. “She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.” At the very moment the Holy Family is in the Temple, she comes, praises God, “and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.” A lifetime of hidden prayer ends in joyful witness.

Then the family returns to Nazareth, where “the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom.” Paul thanks God that the Corinthians “have been enriched in him, in speech and knowledge of every kind”, so that they are “not lacking in any spiritual gift” as they wait for the Lord. God is faithful; he gives his people what they need to grow. Anna in old age and the Child in his youth both show that every stage of life can be full of God.
outline: Ask: who is an elderly person whose prayer has carried your family?
She speaks to all who wait.
Nazareth and the gifts of grace.
“The favor of God was upon him.”
live: Honour the praying elders
Thank a grandparent or elderly parishioner for their prayers.
Grow in wisdom (Luke 2:40)
Choose one spiritual book to read slowly this year.
2027-01-02.prayer: Lord Jesus, you grew in wisdom at Nazareth, and Anna proclaimed you to all who waited. Make me faithful in prayer like her, and help me to grow in your grace all through this year. Amen.
altar: Anna spent her life in the Temple. In the Holy Qurbana we too stand before the Lord; our faithful presence, Sunday after Sunday, becomes witness.

2027-01-04.title: Second Monday of Nativity
2027-01-04.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Whatever is born of God conquers the world
The Son does what he sees the Father doing
2027-01-04.verse: for whatever is born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.
theo: In these last days of Nativity the Church asks who the Child is. Jesus answers in the Gospel: “the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.” This is not weakness but perfect unity. The Son gives life as the Father gives life, and judges as the Father has entrusted to him, “so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father.” The Child of Bethlehem is worthy of the same worship as the Father.

St John draws out what this means for believers: “Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God.” Faith is a new birth. And this new birth is strong: “whatever is born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.” The world with its fears, temptations and pressures does not have the last word over a child of God.
outline: Ask: what in the world around you seems stronger than your faith?
Point 2 · The Son and the Father
One in work, one in honour.
The victory that overcomes the world.
“This is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.”
live: Honour the Son (John 5:23)
Make a slow, reverent Sign of the Cross each time you pray today.
Overcome by faith (1 John 5:4)
Face one fear today with an act of faith: Jesus, I trust in you.
2027-01-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, eternal Son of the Father, you do the works of the Father and give life to whom you will. I believe that you are the Christ; let this faith be my victory over every fear and temptation. Glory to you with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we give glory to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit together. The Son receives the same honour as the Father.

2027-01-05.title: Second Tuesday of Nativity · Eve of Denha
2027-01-05.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Moses faithful as a servant, Christ as a son
2027-01-05.alt: Season of Nativity. Readings from the Second Set (2023–24 calendar). Tonight many families keep the Denha customs: lamps on plantain stems (pindikuthi) and the evening bath recalling the Jordan (rakkuli).
2027-01-05.verse: Christ, however, was faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.
theo: On the eve of Denha the Church sets two great figures side by side. Hebrews honours Moses: he “was faithful in all God's house as a servant.” But Jesus is greater, “faithful over God's house as a son”, as the builder is greater than the house. And then a surprise: “we are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.” The house of God is not only a building; it is the people who keep faith.

In the Gospel the priests and Levites question John at the Jordan. He refuses every great title: he is not the Messiah, nor Elijah, nor the prophet. He is a voice, and he baptises only with water: “Among you stands one whom you do not know.” Tomorrow that unknown one will come down into the Jordan and be revealed by the Father's voice and the Spirit. Our ancestors in Kerala kept this night with lights on plantain stems, crying “El Paiya”, God is light, and with a bath in river or pond recalling the Jordan. Tonight let us prepare our hearts to see him.
outline: Ask: what do the lights and the bath of the Denha eve mean?
Point 3 · One whom you do not know
live: Keep the Denha eve
Light a lamp at home tonight and pray: Christ, light of the world, shine on our family.
Hold firm (Hebrews 3:6)
Renew one good resolution you have let slip.
2027-01-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, faithful Son over God's house, John prepared your way at the Jordan. On this holy night make our home your house, and let us hold firm in hope until we see your glory. Amen.
altar: The Church gathered for the Holy Qurbana is God's house built of living stones. Christ is its faithful Son and builder.

2027-01-07.title: First Thursday of Denha
2027-01-07.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Christ is proclaimed in every way
He must increase, but I must decrease
2027-01-07.verse: What does it matter? Just this, that Christ is proclaimed in every way, whether out of false motives or true; and in that I rejoice.
theo: The day after Denha the Church listens to two men who were glad when Christ was made known, whatever it cost them. Paul writes from prison, yet his letter is full of joy: “what has happened to me has actually helped to spread the gospel.” His chains have become a sermon to the imperial guard, and other believers have grown bolder. Some preach Christ out of rivalry, hoping to hurt Paul; he does not mind: “Christ is proclaimed in every way… and in that I rejoice.”

John the Baptist shows the same freedom when his disciples complain that everyone is going to Jesus: “He must increase, but I must decrease.” The friend of the bridegroom rejoices at the bridegroom's voice. In the season of Denha, when Christ is manifested to the world, the Church asks us to check our hearts: do we rejoice when Christ is known, even through others, even at our expense?
outline: Ask: how do you react when someone else does the good work you hoped to do?
John's joy as the bridegroom's friend.
“Christ is proclaimed in every way… and in that I rejoice.”
live: Offer your chains (Philippians 1:12)
Offer one hardship today for the spread of the Gospel.
Rejoice in others' good (John 3:29)
Congratulate sincerely someone in the parish whose work is praised.
2027-01-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, manifested at the Jordan, let your name be proclaimed in every way. Free me from envy and rivalry; let me rejoice when you increase, even if I decrease. Amen.
altar: The Holy Qurbana proclaims the death and resurrection of the Lord until he comes. Every Qurbana, in every parish, is Christ proclaimed: we rejoice in all of them.

2027-01-08.title: First Friday of Denha · Commemoration of St John the Baptist
2027-01-08.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: I appoint you over nations, to pluck up and to pull down
James is killed; Peter is freed
The beheading of John the Baptist
2027-01-08.alt: Season of Denha. The Third Qudasha is used today.
2027-01-08.verse: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the LORD.
theo: On the Fridays of Denha the Church honours the great witnesses who made Christ known. The first is John the Baptist, who saw the heavens open over Jesus at the Jordan. Today's readings form a gallery of prophetic courage. Nathan goes to King David after his adultery and murder and, through a simple story, leads him to condemn himself; then he says: “You are the man!” Jeremiah, young and afraid, is told: “Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you.”

John paid the price of this courage. He told Herod plainly, “It is not lawful for you to have her.” Herod imprisoned him, and at a drunken birthday banquet, to keep a foolish oath, had him beheaded. In Acts, King Herod Agrippa kills James with the sword and arrests Peter; “the church prayed fervently to God for him”, and an angel leads Peter out. Some witnesses are freed, some are killed; all are held by God. In a world where power often silences conscience, the Baptist's head on a platter is a question to every Christian: will I speak the truth with love, whatever it costs?
outline: Ask: when was the last time you said a hard truth with love?
Nathan's courage leads David to repentance.
Jeremiah and John, consecrated before birth.
“I am with you to deliver you.”
live: Speak the truth with love
Correct one wrong gently and honestly, instead of keeping silent.
Pray for the persecuted (Acts 12:5)
Pray today for Christians imprisoned or threatened for their faith.
2027-01-08.prayer: O God, you sent John the Baptist to prepare the way of your Son and to bear witness to the truth even to death. Give us courage like Nathan, Jeremiah and John, to speak the truth with love, and keep your persecuted Church in your hand. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The Third Qudasha is used today. At the altar we unite ourselves with the witnesses who offered their lives with Christ.

2027-01-09.title: First Saturday of Denha
2027-01-09.readTitle: Readings of the day (Second Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Holy is the Lord God the Almighty
Are you the one who is to come?
2027-01-09.verse: And he answered them, “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them.
theo: From prison John the Baptist sends two disciples to ask Jesus: “Are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another?” Even the great witness has a moment of darkness. Perhaps he expected a Messiah of fire and judgement. Jesus does not argue. He shows what he is doing: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor hear good news. These are the signs Isaiah promised (Isaiah 35:5–6; 61:1). And he adds: “blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me.”

The epistle opens a door in heaven. John the seer sees a throne, a rainbow, twenty-four elders and four living creatures who “Day and night without ceasing… sing, ‘Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come.’” The Church on earth joins this song in every Qurbana. When we doubt, as John did in prison, we look at the works of Christ among the poor and we lift our eyes to the throne: he is the one who is to come.
outline: Ask: have you ever doubted, even after years of faith?
Doubt in the dark of prison.
Jesus answers with deeds of mercy.
“Blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me.”
live: Bring your doubts to Jesus
Tell Jesus honestly any doubt you carry, as John did.
Be a sign (Luke 7:22)
Do one work of mercy today so that someone sees Christ at work.
2027-01-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, you answered John's doubt with deeds of mercy. When I am in darkness, show me your works, lift my eyes to your throne, and let me join the angels' song: Holy, holy, holy. Amen.
altar: In the Holy Qurbana we sing “Holy, holy, holy” with the angels and the living creatures. Heaven's worship and ours are one.

quick: The name Jesus means “the Lord saves”.
God calls each of us by name.
Through humility and the Cross, Jesus received the name above every name.
2027-01-01.action: Pray the Jesus Prayer ten times each morning this year.
2027-01-01.question: Do I call on the name of Jesus with faith, or only out of habit?
catechism: The second commandment: the name of the Lord is holy.
kidsaint: He listened to the angel and gave the baby the name Jesus. Lesson: we say Jesus' name with love, never in anger.
2027-01-01.special: Holy Name of Jesus (Circumcision). New Year's Day. Last Friday of Nativity: Divine Motherhood of Mary.
term: Jesus (Yeshua) means “the LORD saves”; the name that is above every name (Philippians 2:9; CCC 432).

family.explain: An angel told Joseph in a dream: Mary will have a son, and you will call him Jesus, because he will save people from their sins.
family.intention: We pray that Jesus will bless every day of this new year for our family.
family.ask: Ask: “Do you know what your name means? Let us find out together.”

illus: An old man in a Kuttanad parish could no longer remember his children's names after a stroke. But each evening, when his daughter began the family prayer, he joined in clearly at one word: Ee-sho. The Name he had prayed for eighty years stayed when everything else was fading.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your Name is above every name. We gather in your Name at the start of this new year. Bless us, save us and keep us. Amen.
share: “I have called you by name, you are mine” (Isaiah 43:1). How does it feel to be known by name by God?
“You are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people” (Matthew 1:21). From what do I need Jesus to save me this year?
Every knee should bend at the name of Jesus (Philippians 2:10). How do I honour his Name in my speech?
pm.resp: Jesus, Saviour, have mercy on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the Name of Jesus to all peoples.
For our families, that this new year may be lived in the Name of Jesus.
For those who take the Lord's Name in vain, that they may come to love it.
For mothers, through the prayers of the Mother of God.
For our group, that we may call on Jesus in every need.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, at the start of this year we place our lives under your holy Name. Save us from sin, guard us from harm, and lead us with Mary your Mother to the Father. Amen.

quick: Those who stay near God shine and learn to listen.
Jesus' first words: I must be in my Father's house.
Our life offered to God is our spiritual worship.
2027-01-03.action: Begin your prayer this week with: Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening.
2027-01-03.question: Where do I search for Jesus when I have lost him?
kidsaint: A Kerala priest who started schools next to churches so that every child could learn. Lesson: study well and use your learning to help others.
2027-01-03.special: Second Sunday of Nativity. St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. Denha on Wednesday.
term: Jesus' name for the Temple (Luke 2:49): the place of the Father's presence, and finally his own Body and the Church.

family.explain: When Jesus was twelve, he stayed in the Temple. Mary and Joseph searched for three days and found him listening to the teachers. Jesus went home and obeyed them.
family.intention: We pray for children and parents, that they may understand each other.
family.ask: Ask: “What questions about God would you like to ask?”

illus: At Mannanam, St Chavara insisted that every new church have a school beside it, a 'pallikkoodam'. Many of the first pupils were poor children who had never held a book. Generations later, Kerala's literacy owes much to that simple rule: the Father's house and the school side by side.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were found in your Father's house, listening and asking questions. Speak to us now, for your servants are listening. Amen.
share: “Speak, for your servant is listening” (1 Samuel 3:10). How do I listen to God?
“Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?” (Luke 2:49). Where do I find Jesus when I have lost him?
“Present your bodies as a living sacrifice” (Romans 12:1). What can I offer God this week?
pm.resp: Speak, Lord, your servants are listening.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a house where all find the Father.
For parents who worry about their children.
For children and teenagers, that they may grow in wisdom and grace.
For teachers and schools, through the prayers of St Chavara.
For our group, that we may listen to God's word and do it.
pm.close: Heavenly Father, your Son grew in wisdom and favour in the home of Nazareth. Make our homes places of prayer and obedience, and transform us by the renewing of our minds. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At the Jordan the Holy Trinity is revealed.
God comes down, no longer in terror but in tenderness.
Denha calls us to remember and live our Baptism.
2027-01-06.action: Find out your baptismal date and keep it like a birthday.
2027-01-06.question: Do I live as a beloved child of God?
kidsaint: He baptised Jesus in the river Jordan and saw the Holy Spirit come down like a dove. Lesson: you too were baptised; you are God's beloved child.
2027-01-06.special: Denha: Epiphany and Baptism of the Lord. Day of obligation. Third Qudasha. Beginning of the Season of Denha.
term: Syriac for dawn or manifestation: the revelation of the Holy Trinity at Jesus' Baptism in the Jordan.

family.explain: Jesus went into the river Jordan and John baptised him. The sky opened, the Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and God the Father said: you are my Son, I love you!
family.intention: We pray for all who will be baptised this year.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we know the day each of us was baptised? Let us find out.”

illus: A family in Changanassery keeps a small book with the baptismal date of each child. On that date there is no party, but a candle is lit at dinner and the child renews the baptismal promises. The children say it is their favourite day of the year.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, on this feast of Denha you went down into the Jordan and the heavens opened. Open heaven over us as we gather, and pour out your Spirit. Amen.
share: The LORD descended upon Sinai in fire (Exodus 19:18). How do I experience God's holiness?
“You are my Son, the Beloved” (Mark 1:11). Do I believe God says this to me?
“Rekindle the gift of God that is within you” (2 Timothy 1:6). What gift of God in me has grown cold?
pm.resp: Christ, our Light, shine on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may shine with the light of the Holy Trinity.
For all baptised Christians, that they may live as children of light.
For catechumens and those preparing for Baptism.
For those who have abandoned the faith received in Baptism.
For our group, that the Spirit may rekindle God's gifts in us.
pm.close: Father, at the Jordan you declared Jesus your beloved Son and anointed him with the Spirit. Keep us faithful to our Baptism, and make our lives shine with your light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Anna prayed night and day for a lifetime.
She proclaimed the Child to all who were waiting.
Jesus grew in wisdom, and God enriches us with every gift.
2027-01-02.action: Thank a grandparent or elderly parishioner for their prayers.
2027-01-02.question: Am I faithful in prayer even when nothing seems to happen?

family.explain: Old Anna prayed in the Temple every day. When she saw baby Jesus, she was so happy that she told everyone about him.
family.intention: We pray for grandparents and elderly people who pray for us.
family.ask: Ask: “Who prays for our family? Let us thank them.”

illus: In a Thrissur parish an old widow sat in the same corner of the church for forty years, rosary in hand. When she died, the parish priest said at her funeral: most of the vocations from this parish came after she began praying for them. No one had known.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Anna waited for you with fasting and prayer and then spoke of you to everyone. Teach us to pray faithfully and to witness joyfully. Amen.
share: Anna prayed night and day (Luke 2:37). What helps me to pray faithfully?
She spoke of the child to all who were waiting (Luke 2:38). To whom can I speak about Jesus?
The child grew and became strong (Luke 2:40). How have I grown in faith this past year?
interc: For widows and the elderly, that they may know their prayer is precious.
For those who wait for God's answer.
For children and young people, that they may grow in wisdom and grace.
For our parish, that it may be rich in every spiritual gift.
For our group, that we may pray night and day.
pm.close: Lord God, you rewarded Anna's long prayer with the sight of your Son. Keep us faithful in prayer and make us glad witnesses of Jesus. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Whoever believes that Jesus is the Christ is born of God.
The Son does what the Father does and deserves the same honour.
Our faith is the victory that conquers the world.
2027-01-04.action: Face one fear today with an act of faith.
2027-01-04.question: Do I honour Jesus as I honour the Father?

family.explain: Jesus said: I do what I see my Father doing, because the Father loves me. Jesus and the Father always work together.
family.intention: We pray that our family may always work together in love.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing do we learn by watching our parents?”

illus: A young carpenter in Ernakulam learned his trade by watching his father for years. Customers said they could not tell which chair was made by the father and which by the son. Jesus says the same about himself and the Father: whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of the Father, you give life to whom you will. Give us your life as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God (1 John 5:1). What does being born of God mean for me?
The Son does what he sees the Father doing (John 5:19). What do I see God doing in my life?
Faith conquers the world (1 John 5:4). Where do I need faith to win?
interc: For the Church, that she may honour the Son as she honours the Father.
For those whose faith is weak or tested.
For fathers, that their children may learn from their example.
For those who feel defeated by the world.
For our group, that our faith may become victory.
pm.close: Father, your Son does your works and gives life. Make us your children by faith, and let our faith overcome the world. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Moses was faithful as a servant; Christ as the Son.
We are God's house if we hold firm in hope.
John points to the one standing among us, unknown.
2027-01-05.action: Light a lamp at home tonight and pray for your family.
2027-01-05.question: Is my life a house where Christ is welcome?

family.explain: John the Baptist said: someone great is among you, and I am not worthy to untie his sandal. Tomorrow we celebrate when Jesus was baptised.
family.intention: We pray that our home may be full of the light of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our home be a house of God?”

illus: In a village near Pala, an old man still plants a plantain stem in his courtyard each Denha eve and sets small lamps on it. His grandchildren, home from Bengaluru and Dubai, gather round as he calls out “El Paiya!” He says: I cannot preach, but I can light a lamp and tell them who the Light is.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you stood among the crowds at the Jordan, and they did not know you. Let us know you tonight, and make our hearts your house. Amen.
share: Moses was faithful as a servant (Hebrews 3:5). Who has been a faithful servant of God in my life?
We are his house (Hebrews 3:6). How can my family become God's house?
Among you stands one whom you do not know (John 1:26). Where is Jesus standing near me, unrecognised?
pm.resp: Christ our light, shine on us.
interc: For the Church, God's house, that she may stand firm in hope.
For families keeping the Denha eve, that their lamps may be signs of faith.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism.
For those who do not yet recognise Christ among them.
For our group, that we may prepare our hearts for Denha.
pm.close: Father, tomorrow your Son is revealed at the Jordan. Make our homes your dwelling, and let us hold firm the hope we have in him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul's chains helped to spread the Gospel.
He rejoiced whenever Christ was proclaimed.
John rejoiced that Jesus increased while he decreased.
2027-01-07.action: Congratulate sincerely someone whose good work is praised.
2027-01-07.question: Do I rejoice when Christ is made known through others?

family.explain: St Paul was in prison, but he was happy because more and more people were hearing about Jesus. Even in trouble, God can do good things.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are in prison for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “Has something hard ever turned into something good for us?”

illus: A catechism teacher in Thrissur was moved from the senior class she loved to teach the youngest children. She felt hurt, but she accepted. Years later three of those little ones became priests and sisters, and each named her as the first who taught them to love Jesus.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were revealed at the Jordan. Let your name be proclaimed everywhere, and free us from envy. Amen.
share: What has happened to me has helped to spread the gospel (Philippians 1:12). Can a hardship of mine become good news?
Christ is proclaimed, and in that I rejoice (Philippians 1:18). Do I rejoice in others' success in ministry?
He must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30). Where must I decrease?
pm.resp: Lord, let your name be proclaimed.
interc: For Christians in prison for their faith.
For preachers and catechists, that they may seek Christ's glory and not their own.
For parishes divided by rivalry.
For those whose suffering can become witness.
For our group, that Christ may increase in us.
pm.close: Father, let your Son be proclaimed in every way. Free us from rivalry and make us glad witnesses. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Nathan's courage led David to repentance.
John the Baptist died for speaking the truth.
The Church's prayer freed Peter from prison.
2027-01-08.action: Correct one wrong gently and honestly today.
2027-01-08.question: Do I stay silent when I should speak the truth with love?

family.explain: John the Baptist told King Herod that he was doing wrong. Herod put John in prison. John was brave because he loved God and the truth.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who suffer for their faith.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard to tell the truth? How can we be brave?”

illus: In 1986 a young Syro-Malabar priest in a North Indian mission spoke out against a landlord who was cheating poor tribal labourers. He received threats and was transferred for his safety. Years later the labourers' children, now educated, invited him back as chief guest. They said: you were our John the Baptist.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, John the Baptist prepared your way and bore witness to the truth even to death. Give us his courage and his humility. Amen.
share: Nathan said, “You are the man!” (2 Samuel 12:7). Do I accept correction when I am wrong?
“Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you” (Jeremiah 1:8). What fear keeps me from witnessing?
The church prayed fervently for Peter (Acts 12:5). For whom should our group pray fervently?
interc: For the persecuted Church, especially in Asia and Africa.
For prophets in our time who speak the truth to power.
For rulers, that they may listen to conscience.
For those who have been silenced, threatened or imprisoned.
For our group, that we may speak the truth with love.
pm.close: Lord God, John the Baptist gave his life for the truth. Strengthen us to witness to Christ without fear, and protect all who suffer for his name. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Even John the Baptist had a moment of doubt.
Jesus answers with deeds: the blind see, the poor hear good news.
Heaven sings without ceasing: Holy, holy, holy.
2027-01-09.action: Do one work of mercy today so that someone sees Christ at work.
2027-01-09.question: Do I bring my doubts honestly to Jesus?

family.explain: John asked: Jesus, are you really the one God sent? Jesus said: look! The blind see, the lame walk, the sick are healed, the poor hear good news.
family.intention: We pray for people who are blind, lame or sick.
family.ask: Ask: “How can people see Jesus at work in our family?”

illus: A young woman from Kottayam working as a nurse in Germany lost her faith during the pandemic. One night a dying patient asked her to pray with him. She did, haltingly, and saw his face fill with peace. She said later: I asked God if he was real, and he answered through a dying man.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, John asked if you were the one to come, and you answered with deeds of love. Answer our doubts too, and let us sing Holy, holy, holy. Amen.
share: Are you the one who is to come? (Luke 7:19). What questions do I bring to Jesus?
Go and tell John what you have seen (Luke 7:22). What have I seen Jesus do?
Holy, holy, holy (Revelation 4:8). How does the worship of heaven change my view of my troubles?
pm.resp: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord.
interc: For those struggling with doubt, that they may meet Christ in his works of mercy.
For the blind, the lame and the sick.
For the poor, that they may hear good news through the Church.
For prisoners, as John was.
For our group, that our worship may join heaven's song.
pm.close: Father, your Son showed John the signs of his kingdom. Show us his works, strengthen our faith, and let us praise you with all the hosts of heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed new year to you all. On this first day of the year the Church does not begin with our plans but with a Name: the Holy Name of Jesus. Eight days after his birth, the Child was circumcised and named Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived (Luke 2:21).

In the Bible a name is never only a label. In the first reading God changes Abram's name to Abraham, father of a multitude, and gives him the covenant (Genesis 17:5). And through Isaiah he says to his people: I have called you by name, you are mine (Isaiah 43:1). Each of us was called by name at Baptism. God knows you, not as a number, but by name.

The name Jesus means the Lord saves. The angel says to Joseph: you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21). We may want many things from the new year: health, a job, success for our children. Jesus comes first to save us from sin, the root of every other sorrow.

St Paul tells us how this Name was won. Christ Jesus emptied himself, took the form of a slave, humbled himself and became obedient to death on a cross. Therefore God highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name (Philippians 2:7–9). The way to glory is the way of humility.

Today is also the last Friday of Nativity, when our Church honours the Divine Motherhood of Mary. She who gave Jesus his human flesh is truly the Mother of God, and she stands with the Apostles in prayer (Acts 1:14). Let us begin this year with her.

So let us make a simple resolution: to call on the Name of Jesus every day. Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner. Let this Name be on our lips in joy and in trouble, and this year will be blessed. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Jesus' name day! The name Jesus means God saves us. Let us say his name with love every day.
Do you know your own name's meaning? Ask your parents tonight, and thank God for calling you by name.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this Second Sunday of Nativity all our readings take place in the presence of God. Moses comes down from Mount Sinai after forty days, and the skin of his face shines because he has been talking with God (Exodus 34:29). He does not even know it.

The boy Samuel sleeps in the temple where the ark of God is. Three times the Lord calls him, and three times he runs to old Eli. Finally he learns to say: speak, for your servant is listening (1 Samuel 3:10). Those who stay near God are changed by him, and they learn to listen.

In the Gospel Jesus is twelve. After the Passover he stays behind in Jerusalem. For three days Mary and Joseph search for him with great anxiety. Every parent here knows that feeling. They find him in the Temple, sitting among the teachers, listening and asking questions.

His first words in the Gospel are: why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house? (Luke 2:49). At twelve, Jesus knows who his Father is. And yet he goes down with them to Nazareth and is obedient to them, and grows in wisdom and in years and in favour with God and people (Luke 2:51–52). Holiness does not despise ordinary family life; it is lived there.

St Paul tells us how to live this: present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship. Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your minds (Romans 12:1–2). Our whole life becomes worship.

Today we also remember St Kuriakose Elias Chavara, a son of our Church who stayed close to God in prayer and built schools beside churches so that children could grow in wisdom. Let us ask for his spirit: to listen to God, to love the Father's house, and to serve our families with obedience and love. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus was twelve, Mary and Joseph lost him for three days! They found him in the Temple, learning about God. Then he went home and obeyed them.
Let us love to come to church, the Father's house, and let us obey our parents with a smile.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed feast of Denha to you. Denha means dawn, rising, manifestation. Our Church celebrates today the Baptism of Jesus in the Jordan, because there the whole mystery of God was revealed.

Look at the scene in Mark. Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptised by John. Just as he is coming up out of the water, he sees the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him. And a voice comes from heaven: you are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased (Mark 1:10–11). Son, Spirit and Father: the Holy Trinity is revealed.

The first reading takes us to Sinai. The LORD descended upon it in fire; the mountain shook violently, and the people had to keep away (Exodus 19:18). At the Jordan God comes down again, but now so gently: a dove, a voice of love, a man standing in the river among sinners. What was terrifying at Sinai becomes tender at the Jordan.

Why was Jesus baptised? He had no sin. He went down into the water to stand with us sinners and to sanctify the waters for our Baptism. The prophet Joel had promised: I will pour out my spirit on all flesh (Joel 2:28). That outpouring begins with Jesus and reaches us in Baptism and Confirmation.

Our ancestors kept this feast beautifully. They lit lamps on plantain stems and walked around crying El Paiya, God is light. On the eve they bathed in rivers and ponds, remembering the Jordan. These customs said: we are baptised; we are children of light.

St Paul tells Timothy: rekindle the gift of God that is within you (2 Timothy 1:6). Many of us were baptised as infants and rarely think of it. Today, let us remember: God has said to you, you are my beloved son, my beloved daughter. Let us live as people who have heard that voice. Amen.
kids: Children, today is Denha! Jesus was baptised in the river Jordan. The Holy Spirit came down like a dove, and God said: you are my beloved Son!
When you were baptised, God said the same to you: you are my beloved child. Ask your parents when your Baptism day is!

homily: Dear friends, at the end of the Presentation story Luke tells us about Anna. She was a prophet, widowed after only seven years of marriage, and now eighty-four years old. She never left the Temple but worshipped there with fasting and prayer night and day (Luke 2:36–37).

Imagine those decades of prayer. No visions, no headlines, just faithfulness. And then one day, at that very moment, she comes and sees the Child. She begins to praise God and to speak about him to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem (Luke 2:38).
Anna teaches us that no prayer is wasted. Many grandmothers and grandfathers in our parishes are Annas: their hidden prayer carries families, vocations and the whole Church.

St Paul thanks God that the Corinthians are not lacking in any spiritual gift as they wait for the Lord (1 Corinthians 1:7). God is faithful. In Nazareth the child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom (Luke 2:40). Let us ask for Anna's faithfulness and the Child's wisdom in this new year. Amen.
kids: Children, Anna was a very old lady who prayed every day. When she saw baby Jesus, she told everyone! Let us thank our grandparents who pray for us.

homily: Dear friends, in these final days of the Nativity season the Church asks: who is this Child? Jesus answers in the Gospel: the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise (John 5:19).

This is the language of perfect unity. Jesus gives life as the Father gives life. He is entrusted with judgement. And all must honour the Son just as they honour the Father (John 5:23). The Child in the manger is worthy of the same worship as the Father.
St John tells us what this means for us. Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God (1 John 5:1). Faith is not only an opinion; it is a new birth.

And this new birth is powerful: whatever is born of God conquers the world. This is the victory that conquers the world, our faith (1 John 5:4). Fears, temptations and the pressures of the world do not have the last word over a child of God.
As Denha approaches, let us renew our faith in Jesus, the Son of the Father, and live this week as children who have already won. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus always does what his Father does, because they love each other. Watch the good things your parents do, and do the same!

homily: Dear friends, tonight is the eve of Denha. The letter to the Hebrews compares Moses and Jesus. Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant. Christ was faithful over God's house as a son (Hebrews 3:5–6). The servant is honoured; the Son is the heir and builder.

Then Hebrews says something wonderful: we are his house, if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope (Hebrews 3:6). We are not only visitors in God's house. We are the house, the living temple where God dwells.

In the Gospel John the Baptist is questioned. Who are you? He refuses every title. He is only a voice. And he says: among you stands one whom you do not know (John 1:26). Jesus is already there in the crowd, unknown.

Tomorrow that hidden one will step into the Jordan, and the heavens will open. Our ancestors kept this night with lamps on plantain stems, crying El Paiya, God is light, and with a bath that recalled the Jordan. Let us light a lamp in our hearts tonight, and prepare to see him. Amen.
kids: Children, tonight is the eve of Denha! In many homes people light lamps and say: God is light! Light a lamp with your family and say thank you to Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, on the day after Denha we hear from Paul in prison. You would expect complaints. Instead he writes: what has happened to me has actually helped to spread the gospel (Philippians 1:12). The whole imperial guard knows why he is in chains, and other believers have become bolder.

Some, he says, preach Christ out of envy, trying to make his imprisonment harder. Paul's answer is astonishing: what does it matter? Christ is proclaimed in every way, and in that I rejoice (Philippians 1:18). He cares more about Christ being known than about his own reputation.

John the Baptist has the same heart. When his disciples complain that everyone is going to Jesus, he says: he must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30). He is the friend of the bridegroom, and his joy is complete.

In the season of Denha Christ is manifested to the world. Let us check our hearts. Envy and rivalry can enter even church work. May we rejoice whenever Christ is proclaimed, by whoever proclaims him. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul was in prison, but he was happy because people were hearing about Jesus. Let us be happy when others do good things too!

homily: Dear friends, on the Fridays of Denha the Church remembers the witnesses of Christ. Today we honour John the Baptist, who saw the heavens open at the Jordan. The readings show us what a prophet looks like.

Nathan goes to King David after his sin with Bathsheba and the murder of Uriah. He tells a story of a rich man who stole a poor man's only lamb. David is furious. Then Nathan says: you are the man! (2 Samuel 12:7). Courage and wisdom bring the king to repentance.

Jeremiah is young and afraid, but God says: do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you (Jeremiah 1:8). John the Baptist was consecrated even before birth, leaping in his mother's womb before Jesus.
John told Herod: it is not lawful for you to have her (Matthew 14:4). Herod imprisoned him and, at a drunken party, to keep a foolish promise, had him beheaded. Truth spoken with love can be costly.

In Acts, James is killed and Peter imprisoned. But the church prayed fervently to God for him (Acts 12:5), and an angel set him free. Some witnesses are freed, some die, but all are held by God. Let us pray for courage to speak the truth with love, and let us pray fervently for the persecuted Church. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist was very brave. He told the king the truth even when it was dangerous. Let us always tell the truth, kindly and bravely.

homily: Dear friends, from Herod's prison John the Baptist sends two disciples to Jesus with a question: are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another? (Luke 7:19). Even the great prophet who saw the heavens open has a moment of darkness.

Jesus does not scold him and does not argue. He tells the messengers: go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them (Luke 7:22). These are the signs Isaiah promised.
Then he adds: blessed is anyone who takes no offense at me (Luke 7:23). The Messiah does not always act as we expect. He comes in mercy before he comes in judgement.

The epistle opens a door in heaven. Around the throne the living creatures sing day and night: holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come (Revelation 4:8). We join that song at every Qurbana. When doubts come, let us bring them honestly to Jesus, look at his works of mercy, and lift our eyes to his throne. Amen.
kids: Children, even John the Baptist had a question for Jesus. Jesus answered: look at what I do! I help the blind and the sick. You can ask Jesus your questions too.

intro: Theme: “You are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”
The Holy Name at the start of the year: called by name, saved, exalted.

sub: A new name, a new mission.
q: But now thus says the LORD, he who created you, O Jacob, he who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
After eight days had passed, it was time to circumcise the child; and he was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.
points.apply: Learn the meaning of your baptismal name and thank God for it.

sub: Call on him in every need.
q: Then everyone who calls on the name of the LORD shall be saved;
She will bear a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.
points.apply: Pray the Jesus Prayer each morning this year.

q: To me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.
Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend, in heaven and on earth and under the earth,
points.apply: Never use the Lord's name carelessly; bow your head when you hear it.

concl: The year begins with the Name that saves.
With Mary, Mother of God, let us carry this Name into every day.
2027-01-01.resolve: Consecrate the new year to Jesus tonight as a family.

intro: Theme: “Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?”
Near God we shine, listen, and offer ourselves.

points.h: Near God, we shine and listen
q: Now the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”

And all of us, with unveiled faces, seeing the glory of the Lord as though reflected in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another; for this comes from the Lord, the Spirit.
points.apply: Begin each prayer this week with Samuel's words.

q: One thing I asked of the LORD, that will I seek after: to live in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple.
He said to them, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?”
points.apply: Visit the church on a weekday this week.

q: Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
points.apply: Children obey promptly; parents listen patiently.

q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
I appeal to you therefore, brothers and sisters, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
points.apply: Offer your work each morning as a sacrifice to God.

concl: Like Jesus, we belong in the Father's house, and we sanctify our homes by obedience.
St Chavara shows this joined together: prayer, family, education.
2027-01-03.resolve: Prepare for Denha on Wednesday with a family prayer and confession.

intro: Theme: “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
Denha: the dawn of the Trinity's revelation and of our Baptism.

q: Now Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke, because the LORD had descended upon it in fire; the smoke went up like the smoke of a kiln, while the whole mountain shook violently.
And just as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silent adoration today.

q: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.
And a voice came from heaven, “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
points.apply: Make the Sign of the Cross slowly and with faith each time you pray.

sub: Fulfilled in Christ and the Church.
q: Then afterward I will pour out my spirit on all flesh; your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions.
For this reason I remind you to rekindle the gift of God that is within you through the laying on of my hands;
points.apply: Use one gift of God to serve others this month.

q: For with you is the fountain of life; in your light we see light.
but it has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Christ Jesus, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel.
points.apply: Find your baptismal date and celebrate it.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opened, and it has not closed.
We are baptised: let us live as the Father's beloved.
2027-01-06.resolve: Keep holy water at home and bless your family each night.

intro: Theme: “She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.”
Anna's faithfulness and the Child's growth.

sub: Fasting and prayer night and day.
q: Evening and morning and at noon I utter my complaint and moan, and he will hear my voice.
then as a widow to the age of eighty-four. She never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day.
points.apply: Keep a fixed time of prayer every day this year.

sub: She comes at that very moment.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
At that moment she came, and began to praise God and to speak about the child to all who were looking for the redemption of Jerusalem.
points.apply: Speak about Jesus to one person this week.

q: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the Holy One is insight.
God is faithful; by him you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
points.apply: Choose one spiritual book to read this year.

concl: Old Anna and the young Child both show a life full of God.
2027-01-02.resolve: Thank an elderly person for their prayers this week.

intro: Theme: “This is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.”
The Son one with the Father; believers born of God.

sub: Love for the Father includes his children.
q: Is not he your father, who created you, who made you and established you?
Everyone who believes that Jesus is the Christ has been born of God, and everyone who loves the parent loves the child.
points.apply: Thank God today for your Baptism.

points.h: The Son does the Father's works
sub: Honour the Son as the Father.
q: then I was beside him, like a master worker; and I was daily his delight, rejoicing before him always,
Jesus said to them, “Very truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing on his own, but only what he sees the Father doing; for whatever the Father does, the Son does likewise.
points.apply: Pray the Glory Be with full attention each time today.

q: With the LORD on my side I do not fear. What can mortals do to me?
for whatever is born of God conquers the world. And this is the victory that conquers the world, our faith.
points.apply: Make an act of faith whenever fear rises.

concl: The Child is the eternal Son, worthy of all honour.
Born of God, we share his victory.
2027-01-04.resolve: Prepare for Denha by renewing your baptismal promises.

intro: Theme: “We are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.”
Servant and Son; the unknown one among us.

sub: A witness to what would come.
q: Not so with my servant Moses; he is entrusted with all my house.
Now Moses was faithful in all God's house as a servant, to testify to the things that would be spoken later.
points.apply: Thank God for a faithful servant who taught you the faith.

points.h: Christ the Son; we are his house
sub: The builder is greater than the house.
Christ is the Son and heir.
We are the house if we hold firm.
q: He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever.
Christ, however, was faithful over God's house as a son, and we are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.
points.apply: Make one change at home that makes it more a house of God.

points.h: One whom you do not know
sub: The hidden one stands among us.
q: Every valley shall be lifted up, and every mountain and hill be made low; the uneven ground shall become level, and the rough places a plain.
John answered them, “I baptize with water. Among you stands one whom you do not know, the one who is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thong of his sandal.”
points.apply: Light a lamp tonight and pray for those who do not know Christ.

concl: Tomorrow the hidden one is revealed at the Jordan.
Let us be his house, lit and ready.
2027-01-05.resolve: Keep the Denha eve with a lamp and family prayer.

intro: Theme: “Christ is proclaimed in every way… and in that I rejoice.”
Joy without rivalry: Paul in chains, John the friend of the bridegroom.

q: Even though you intended to do harm to me, God intended it for good, in order to preserve a numerous people, as he is doing today.
I want you to know, beloved, that what has happened to me has actually helped to spread the gospel,
points.apply: Offer one hardship today for the Gospel.

q: But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!”
What does it matter? Just this, that Christ is proclaimed in every way, whether out of false motives or true; and in that I rejoice.
points.apply: Pray for a fellow worker you envy.

q: The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low, he also exalts.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Do one hidden act of service this week.

concl: In the season of Denha, Christ is to be manifested, not we.
Joy in his glory heals envy.

intro: Theme: “Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you.”
The Baptist and the prophets: courage for the truth, held by God.

q: Nathan said to David, “You are the man! Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel: I anointed you king over Israel, and I rescued you from the hand of Saul;
For Herod had arrested John, bound him, and put him in prison on account of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, because John had been telling him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
points.apply: Accept one correction this week without defending yourself.

sub: John filled with the Spirit before birth.
God's call is older than our fears.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
for he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He must never drink wine or strong drink; even before his birth he will be filled with the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Pray for unborn children and for the vocations God has prepared.

q: They will fight against you; but they shall not prevail against you, for I am with you, says the LORD, to deliver you.
While Peter was kept in prison, the church prayed fervently to God for him.
points.apply: Pray daily this week for the persecuted Church.

concl: Truth with love, held by God's promise: I am with you.
2027-01-08.resolve: Speak one hard truth this week, gently and with love.

intro: Theme: “Are you the one who is to come?”
John's question, Jesus' answer, heaven's song.

q: Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf unstopped; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy.
and sent them to the Lord to ask, “Are you the one who is to come, or are we to wait for another?”
points.apply: Bring one honest question to Jesus in prayer.

sub: Blessed is the one not offended.
q: the LORD opens the eyes of the blind. The LORD lifts up those who are bowed down; the LORD loves the righteous.

And he answered them, “Go and tell John what you have seen and heard: the blind receive their sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news brought to them.
points.apply: Do one work of mercy today.

sub: We join them at the Qurbana.
q: And one called to another and said: “Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is full of his glory.”

And the four living creatures, each of them with six wings, are full of eyes all around and inside. Day and night without ceasing they sing, “Holy, holy, holy, the Lord God the Almighty, who was and is and is to come.”
points.apply: Sing the Holy, holy, holy at Qurbana with full attention tomorrow.

concl: Christ answers doubt with mercy and lifts our eyes to his throne.
He is the one who is to come.
2027-01-09.resolve: Prepare for Sunday by spending time before the Blessed Sacrament.
